verdict.rationale: Vercel's Fluid compute pricing bills Active CPU only during actual code execution, not during I/O waits such as database or AI model calls, which directly addresses idle-time billing for CPU. However, Provisioned Memory is billed for the entire instance lifetime, including I/O waits, so part of the compute bill still tracks wall-clock time. Missing for 10: memory billed only on active time rather than instance lifetime, independent or hands-on corroboration of the billing behavior.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can pay only for active compute time rather than idle wall-clock time

citations.quote: You are only billed during actual code execution and not during I/O operations
If your function takes 100ms to process data but spends 400ms waiting for a database query, you're only billed for the 100ms of active CPU time.
Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
